dataset_metadata.evaluation_split_method: fraudTrain.csv (held-out 20% test partition withheld from pipeline.fit() using train_test_split test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y)

threshold_analysis.description: Medium Risk Threshold (Flags suspicious transactions for verification)
Standard Decision Boundary (Default binary classification cutoff)
High Risk Threshold (Conservative cutoff minimizing false alarms)

methodology_disclosures.class_imbalance: Severe positive class imbalance (0.579% fraud). Accuracy alone (99.8%) is deceptive because a trivial majority-class predictor achieves 99.42% accuracy. Precision (93.2%), Recall (73.4%), and PR-AUC (88.9%) are the primary reliability benchmarks.
methodology_disclosures.temporal_split_limitation: The held-out evaluation set was partitioned using stratified random sampling (test_size=0.20, random_state=42), matching train_model.py. Transactions from future dates exist in both partitions. An out-of-time (OOT) evaluation on subsequent dates is recommended for strict temporal validation.
methodology_disclosures.account_grouping_limitation: Card numbers (cc_num) were withheld from training features but not grouped during splitting. Transactions from the same synthetic customer appear in both train and test partitions.
methodology_disclosures.inference_gap: The web UI collects transaction amount, channel, and merchant category. Location coordinates and demographic features are held at static median defaults during real-time scoring.
